documents.title: attack-pattern: overview
documents.text: Attack Patterns are a type of TTP that describe ways that adversaries attempt to compromise targets. Attack Patterns are used to help categorize attacks, generalize specific attacks to the patterns that they follow, and provide detailed information about how attacks are performed. An example of an attack pattern is "spear phishing": a common type of attack where an attacker sends a carefully crafted e-mail message to a party with the intent of getting them to click a link or open an attachment to deliver malware. Attack Patterns can also be more specific; spear phishing as practiced by a particular threat actor (e.g., they might generally say that the target won a contest) can also be an Attack Pattern. The Attack Pattern SDO contains textual descriptions of the pattern along with references to externally-defined taxonomies of attacks such as CAPEC [CAPEC ].

documents.title: attack-pattern.type
documents.text: attack-pattern.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be attack-pattern .

documents.title: attack-pattern.external_references
documents.text: attack-pattern.external_references has type list of type external-reference. Its property-table status is optional. A list of external references which refer to non-STIX information. This property MAY be used to provide one or more Attack Pattern identifiers, such as a CAPEC ID. When specifying a CAPEC ID, the source_name property of the external reference MUST be set to capec and the external_id property MUST be formatted as CAPEC-[id] .

documents.title: attack-pattern.name
documents.text: attack-pattern.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify the Attack Pattern.

documents.title: attack-pattern.description
documents.text: attack-pattern.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Attack Pattern, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: attack-pattern.aliases
documents.text: attack-pattern.aliases has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Alternative names used to identify this Attack Pattern.

documents.title: attack-pattern.kill_chain_phases
documents.text: attack-pattern.kill_chain_phases has type list of type kill-chain-phase. Its property-table status is optional. The list of Kill Chain Phases for which this Attack Pattern is used.

documents.title: attack-pattern: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for attack-pattern are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: campaign: overview
documents.text: A Campaign is a grouping of adversarial behaviors that describes a set of malicious activities or attacks (sometimes called waves) that occur over a period of time against a specific set of targets. Campaigns usually have well defined objectives and may be part of an Intrusion Set. Campaigns are often attributed to an intrusion set and threat actors. The threat actors may reuse known infrastructure from the intrusion set or may set up new infrastructure specific for conducting that campaign.

documents.title: campaign.type
documents.text: campaign.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be campaign .

documents.title: campaign.name
documents.text: campaign.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify the Campaign.

documents.title: campaign.description
documents.text: campaign.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Campaign, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: campaign.aliases
documents.text: campaign.aliases has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Alternative names used to identify this Campaign

documents.title: campaign.first_seen
documents.text: campaign.first_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Campaign was first seen. A summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are earlier than the first seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data.

documents.title: campaign.last_seen
documents.text: campaign.last_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Campaign was last seen. A summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are later than the last seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data. If this property and the first_seen property are both defined, then this property MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the first_seen property.

documents.title: campaign.objective
documents.text: campaign.objective has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The Campaign’s primary goal, objective, desired outcome, or intended effect — what the Threat Actor or Intrusion Set hopes to accomplish with this Campaign.

documents.title: campaign: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for campaign are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: course-of-action: overview
documents.text: Note: The Course of Action object in STIX 2.1 is a stub. It is included to support basic use cases (such as sharing prose courses of action) but does not support the ability to represent automated courses of action or contain properties to represent metadata about courses of action. Future STIX 2 releases will expand it to include these capabilities. A Course of Action is an action taken either to prevent an attack or to respond to an attack that is in progress. It may describe technical, automatable responses (applying patches, reconfiguring firewalls) but can also describe higher level actions like employee training or policy changes. For example, a course of action to mitigate a vulnerability could describe applying the patch that fixes it.

documents.title: course-of-action.type
documents.text: course-of-action.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be course-of-action .

documents.title: course-of-action.name
documents.text: course-of-action.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify the Course of Action.

documents.title: course-of-action.description
documents.text: course-of-action.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Course of Action, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: course-of-action.action
documents.text: course-of-action.action has type RESERVED. Its property-table status is reserved. RESERVED – To capture structured/automated courses of action.

documents.title: course-of-action: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for course-of-action are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: grouping: overview
documents.text: A Grouping object explicitly asserts that the referenced STIX Objects have a shared context, unlike a STIX Bundle (which explicitly conveys no context). A Grouping object should not be confused with an intelligence product, which should be conveyed via a STIX Report. A STIX Grouping object might represent a set of data that, in time, given sufficient analysis, would mature to convey an incident or threat report as a STIX Report object. For example, a Grouping could be used to characterize an ongoing investigation into a security event or incident. A Grouping object could also be used to assert that the referenced STIX Objects are related to an ongoing analysis process, such as when a threat analyst is collaborating with others in their trust community to examine a series of Campaigns and Indicators. The Grouping SDO contains a list of references to SDOs, SCOs, SROs, and SMOs, along with an explicit statement of the context shared by the content, a textual description, and the name of the grouping.

documents.title: grouping.type
documents.text: grouping.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be grouping .

documents.title: grouping.name
documents.text: grouping.name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A name used to identify the Grouping.

documents.title: grouping.description
documents.text: grouping.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Grouping, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: grouping.context
documents.text: grouping.context has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is required. A short descriptor of the particular context shared by the content referenced by the Grouping. The value for this property SHOULD come from the grouping-context-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: grouping.object_refs
documents.text: grouping.object_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the STIX Objects that are referred to by this Grouping.

documents.title: grouping: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for grouping are: context, created, id, modified, object_refs, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: identity: overview
documents.text: Identities can represent actual individuals, organizations, or groups (e.g., ACME, Inc.) as well as classes of individuals, organizations, systems or groups (e.g., the finance sector). The Identity SDO can capture basic identifying information, contact information, and the sectors that the Identity belongs to. Identity is used in STIX to represent, among other things, targets of attacks, information sources, object creators, and threat actor identities.

documents.title: identity.type
documents.text: identity.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be identity .

documents.title: identity.name
documents.text: identity.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. The name of this Identity. When referring to a specific entity (e.g., an individual or organization), this property SHOULD contain the canonical name of the specific entity.

documents.title: identity.description
documents.text: identity.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Identity, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: identity.roles
documents.text: identity.roles has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. The list of roles that this Identity performs (e.g., CEO, Domain Administrators, Doctors, Hospital, or Retailer). No open vocabulary is yet defined for this property.

documents.title: identity.identity_class
documents.text: identity.identity_class has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The type of entity that this Identity describes, e.g., an individual or organization. The value for this property SHOULD come from the identity-class-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: identity.sectors
documents.text: identity.sectors has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The list of industry sectors that this Identity belongs to. The values for this property SHOULD come from the industry-sector-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: identity.contact_information
documents.text: identity.contact_information has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The contact information (e-mail, phone number, etc.) for this Identity. No format for this information is currently defined by this specification.

documents.title: identity: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for identity are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: incident: overview
documents.text: Note: The Incident object in STIX 2.1 is a stub. It is included to support basic use cases but does not contain properties to represent metadata about incidents. Future STIX 2 releases will expand it to include these capabilities. It is suggested that it is used as an extension point for an Incident object defined using the extension facility described in section 7.3.

documents.title: incident.type
documents.text: incident.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be incident .

documents.title: incident.name
documents.text: incident.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify the Incident.

documents.title: incident.description
documents.text: incident.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Incident, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: incident: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for incident are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: indicator: overview
documents.text: Indicators contain a pattern that can be used to detect suspicious or malicious cyber activity. For example, an Indicator may be used to represent a set of malicious domains and use the STIX Patterning Language (see section 9 ) to specify these domains. The Indicator SDO contains a simple textual description, the Kill Chain Phases that it detects behavior in, a time window for when the Indicator is valid or useful, and a required pattern property to capture a structured detection pattern. Conforming STIX implementations MUST support the STIX Patterning Language as defined in section 9 .

documents.title: indicator.type
documents.text: indicator.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be indicator .

documents.title: indicator.name
documents.text: indicator.name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A name used to identify the Indicator. Producers SHOULD provide this property to help products and analysts understand what this Indicator actually does.

documents.title: indicator.description
documents.text: indicator.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Indicator, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics. Producers SHOULD provide this property to help products and analysts understand what this Indicator actually does.

documents.title: indicator.indicator_types
documents.text: indicator.indicator_types has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. A set of categorizations for this indicator. The values for this property SHOULD come from the indicator-type-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: indicator.pattern
documents.text: indicator.pattern has type string. Its property-table status is required. The detection pattern for this Indicator MAY be expressed as a STIX Pattern as specified in section 9 or another appropriate language such as SNORT, YARA, etc.

documents.title: indicator.pattern_type
documents.text: indicator.pattern_type has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is required. The pattern language used in this indicator. The value for this property SHOULD come from the pattern-type-ov open vocabulary. The value of this property MUST match the type of pattern data included in the pattern property.

documents.title: indicator.pattern_version
documents.text: indicator.pattern_version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The version of the pattern language that is used for the data in the pattern property which MUST match the type of pattern data included in the pattern property. For patterns that do not have a formal specification, the build or code version that the pattern is known to work with SHOULD be used. For the STIX Pattern language, the default value is determined by the specification version of the object. For other languages, the default value SHOULD be the latest version of the patterning language at the time of this object's creation.

documents.title: indicator.valid_from
documents.text: indicator.valid_from has type timestamp. Its property-table status is required. The time from which this Indicator is considered a valid indicator of the behaviors it is related or represents.

documents.title: indicator.valid_until
documents.text: indicator.valid_until has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time at which this Indicator should no longer be considered a valid indicator of the behaviors it is related to or represents. If the valid_until property is omitted, then there is no constraint on the latest time for which the Indicator is valid. This MUST be greater than the timestamp in the valid_from property.

documents.title: indicator.kill_chain_phases
documents.text: indicator.kill_chain_phases has type list of type kill-chain-phase. Its property-table status is optional. The kill chain phase(s) to which this Indicator corresponds.

documents.title: indicator: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for indicator are: created, id, modified, pattern, pattern_type, spec_version, type, valid_from. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: infrastructure: overview
documents.text: The Infrastructure SDO represents a type of TTP and describes any systems, software services and any associated physical or virtual resources intended to support some purpose (e.g., C2 servers used as part of an attack, device or server that are part of defense, database servers targeted by an attack, etc.). While elements of an attack can be represented by other SDOs or SCOs, the Infrastructure SDO represents a named group of related data that constitutes the infrastructure.

documents.title: infrastructure.type
documents.text: infrastructure.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be infrastructure .

documents.title: infrastructure.name
documents.text: infrastructure.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name or characterizing text used to identify the Infrastructure.

documents.title: infrastructure.description
documents.text: infrastructure.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Infrastructure, potentially including its purpose, how it is being used, how it relates to other intelligence activities captured in related objects, and its key characteristics.

documents.title: infrastructure.infrastructure_types
documents.text: infrastructure.infrastructure_types has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The type of infrastructure being described. The values for this property SHOULD come from the infrastructure-type-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: infrastructure.aliases
documents.text: infrastructure.aliases has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Alternative names used to identify this Infrastructure.

documents.title: infrastructure.kill_chain_phases
documents.text: infrastructure.kill_chain_phases has type list of type kill-chain-phase. Its property-table status is optional. The list of Kill Chain Phases for which this Infrastructure is used.

documents.title: infrastructure.first_seen
documents.text: infrastructure.first_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Infrastructure was first seen performing malicious activities.

documents.title: infrastructure.last_seen
documents.text: infrastructure.last_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Infrastructure was last seen performing malicious activities. If this property and the first_seen property are both defined, then this property MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the first_seen property.

documents.title: infrastructure: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for infrastructure are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: intrusion-set: overview
documents.text: An Intrusion Set is a grouped set of adversarial behaviors and resources with common properties that is believed to be orchestrated by a single organization. An Intrusion Set may capture multiple Campaigns or other activities that are all tied together by shared attributes indicating a commonly known or unknown Threat Actor. New activity can be attributed to an Intrusion Set even if the Threat Actors behind the attack are not known. Threat Actors can move from supporting one Intrusion Set to supporting another, or they may support multiple Intrusion Sets. Where a Campaign is a set of attacks over a period of time against a specific set of targets to achieve some objective, an Intrusion Set is the entire attack package and may be used over a very long period of time in multiple Campaigns to achieve potentially multiple purposes.

documents.title: intrusion-set.type
documents.text: intrusion-set.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be intrusion-set .

documents.title: intrusion-set.name
documents.text: intrusion-set.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify this Intrusion Set.

documents.title: intrusion-set.description
documents.text: intrusion-set.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Intrusion Set, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: intrusion-set.aliases
documents.text: intrusion-set.aliases has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Alternative names used to identify this Intrusion Set.

documents.title: intrusion-set.first_seen
documents.text: intrusion-set.first_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Intrusion Set was first seen. A summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are earlier than the first seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data.

documents.title: intrusion-set.last_seen
documents.text: intrusion-set.last_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Intrusion Set was last seen. This property is a summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are later than the last seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data. If this property and the first_seen property are both defined, then this property MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the first_seen property.

documents.title: intrusion-set.goals
documents.text: intrusion-set.goals has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. The high-level goals of this Intrusion Set, namely, what are they trying to do. For example, they may be motivated by personal gain, but their goal is to steal credit card numbers. To do this, they may execute specific Campaigns that have detailed objectives like compromising point of sale systems at a large retailer. Another example: to gain information about latest merger and IPO information from ACME Bank.

documents.title: intrusion-set.resource_level
documents.text: intrusion-set.resource_level has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. This property specifies the organizational level at which this Intrusion Set typically works, which in turn determines the resources available to this Intrusion Set for use in an attack. The value for this property SHOULD come from the attack-resource-level-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: intrusion-set.primary_motivation
documents.text: intrusion-set.primary_motivation has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The primary reason, motivation, or purpose behind this Intrusion Set. The motivation is why the Intrusion Set wishes to achieve the goal (what they are trying to achieve). For example, an Intrusion Set with a goal to disrupt the finance sector in a country might be motivated by ideological hatred of capitalism. The value for this property SHOULD come from the attack-motivation-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: intrusion-set.secondary_motivations
documents.text: intrusion-set.secondary_motivations has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The secondary reasons, motivations, or purposes behind this Intrusion Set. These motivations can exist as an equal or near-equal cause to the primary motivation. However, it does not replace or necessarily magnify the primary motivation, but it might indicate additional context. The position in the list has no significance. The values for this property SHOULD come from the attack-motivation-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: intrusion-set: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for intrusion-set are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: location: overview
documents.text: A Location represents a geographic location. The location may be described as any, some or all of the following: region (e.g., North America), civic address (e.g. New York, US), latitude and longitude. Locations are primarily used to give context to other SDOs. For example, a Location could be used in a relationship to describe that the Bourgeois Swallow intrusion set originates from Eastern Europe.

documents.title: location.type
documents.text: location.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be location .

documents.title: location.name
documents.text: location.name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A name used to identify the Location.

documents.title: location.description
documents.text: location.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A textual description of the Location.

documents.title: location.latitude
documents.text: location.latitude has type float. Its property-table status is optional. The latitude of the Location in decimal degrees. Positive numbers describe latitudes north of the equator, and negative numbers describe latitudes south of the equator. The value of this property MUST be between -90.0 and 90.0, inclusive. If the longitude property is present, this property MUST be present.

documents.title: location.longitude
documents.text: location.longitude has type float. Its property-table status is optional. The longitude of the Location in decimal degrees. Positive numbers describe longitudes east of the prime meridian and negative numbers describe longitudes west of the prime meridian. The value of this property MUST be between -180.0 and 180.0, inclusive. If the latitude property is present, this property MUST be present.

documents.title: location.precision
documents.text: location.precision has type float. Its property-table status is optional. Defines the precision of the coordinates specified by the latitude and longitude properties. This is measured in meters. The actual Location may be anywhere up to precision meters from the defined point. If this property is not present, then the precision is unspecified. If this property is present, the latitude and longitude properties MUST be present.

documents.title: location.region
documents.text: location.region has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The region that this Location describes. The value for this property SHOULD come from the region-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: location.country
documents.text: location.country has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The country that this Location describes. This property SHOULD contain a valid ISO 3166-1 ALPHA-2 Code [ISO3166-1 ].

documents.title: location.administrative_area
documents.text: location.administrative_area has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The state, province, or other sub-national administrative area that this Location describes. This property SHOULD contain a valid ISO 3166-2 Code [ISO3166-2] .

documents.title: location.city
documents.text: location.city has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The city that this Location describes.

documents.title: location.street_address
documents.text: location.street_address has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The street address that this Location describes. This property includes all aspects or parts of the street address. For example, some addresses may have multiple lines including a mailstop or apartment number.

documents.title: location.postal_code
documents.text: location.postal_code has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The postal code for this Location.

documents.title: location: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for location are: created, id, modified, spec_version, type. Additional location constraints apply: supply region, country, or both latitude and longitude. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: malware: overview
documents.text: Malware is a type of TTP that represents malicious code. It generally refers to a program that is inserted into a system, usually covertly. The intent is to compromise the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of the victim's data, applications, or operating system (OS) or otherwise annoy or disrupt the victim. The Malware SDO characterizes, identifies, and categorizes malware instances and families from data that may be derived from analysis. This SDO captures detailed information about how the malware works and what it does. This SDO captures contextual data relevant to sharing Malware data without requiring the full analysis provided by the Malware Analysis SDO.

documents.title: malware.type
documents.text: malware.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be malware .

documents.title: malware.name
documents.text: malware.name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A name used to identify the malware instance or family, as specified by the producer of the SDO. For a malware family the name MUST be defined. If a name for a malware instance is not available, the SHA-256 hash value or sample’s filename MAY be used instead.

documents.title: malware.description
documents.text: malware.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the malware instance or family, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: malware.malware_types
documents.text: malware.malware_types has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. A set of categorizations for the malware being described. The values for this property SHOULD come from the malware-type-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: malware.is_family
documents.text: malware.is_family has type boolean. Its property-table status is required. Whether the object represents a malware family (if true ) or a malware instance (if false ).

documents.title: malware.aliases
documents.text: malware.aliases has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Alternative names used to identify this malware or malware family.

documents.title: malware.kill_chain_phases
documents.text: malware.kill_chain_phases has type list of type kill-chain-phase. Its property-table status is optional. The list of Kill Chain Phases for which this malware can be used.

documents.title: malware.first_seen
documents.text: malware.first_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that the malware instance or family was first seen. This property is a summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are earlier than the first seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data.

documents.title: malware.last_seen
documents.text: malware.last_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that the malware family or malware instance was last seen. This property is a summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are later than the last_seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data. If this property and the first_seen property are both defined, then this property MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the first_seen property.

documents.title: malware.operating_system_refs
documents.text: malware.operating_system_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. The operating systems that the malware family or malware instance is executable on. This applies to virtualized operating systems as well as those running on bare metal. The value of this property MUST be the identifier for a SCO software object.

documents.title: malware.architecture_execution_envs
documents.text: malware.architecture_execution_envs has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The processor architectures (e.g., x86, ARM, etc.) that the malware instance or family is executable on. The values for this property SHOULD come from the processor-architecture-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: malware.implementation_languages
documents.text: malware.implementation_languages has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The programming language(s) used to implement the malware instance or family. The values for this property SHOULD come from the implementation-language-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: malware.capabilities
documents.text: malware.capabilities has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. Any of the capabilities identified for the malware instance or family. The values for this property SHOULD come from the malware-capabilities-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: malware.sample_refs
documents.text: malware.sample_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. The sample_refs property specifies a list of identifier s of the SCO file or artifact objects associated with this malware instance(s) or family. If is_family is false , then all samples listed in sample_refs MUST refer to the same binary data.

documents.title: malware: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for malware are: created, id, is_family, modified, spec_version, type. The name property is additionally required when is_family is true. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: malware-analysis: overview
documents.text: Malware Analysis captures the metadata and results of a particular static or dynamic analysis performed on a malware instance or family. One of result or analysis_sco_refs properties MUST be provided.

documents.title: malware-analysis.type
documents.text: malware-analysis.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be malware-analysis .

documents.title: malware-analysis.product
documents.text: malware-analysis.product has type string. Its property-table status is required. The name of the analysis engine or product that was used. Product names SHOULD be all lowercase with words separated by a dash "-". For cases where the name of a product cannot be specified, a value of "anonymized" MUST be used.

documents.title: malware-analysis.version
documents.text: malware-analysis.version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The version of the analysis product that was used to perform the analysis.

documents.title: malware-analysis.host_vm_ref
documents.text: malware-analysis.host_vm_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. A description of the virtual machine environment used to host the guest operating system (if applicable) that was used for the dynamic analysis of the malware instance or family. If this value is not included in conjunction with the operating_system_ref property, this means that the dynamic analysis may have been performed on bare metal (i.e. without virtualization) or the information was redacted. The value of this property MUST be the identifier for a SCO software object.

documents.title: malware-analysis.operating_system_ref
documents.text: malware-analysis.operating_system_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. The operating system used for the dynamic analysis of the malware instance or family. This applies to virtualized operating systems as well as those running on bare metal. The value of this property MUST be the identifier for a SCO software object.

documents.title: malware-analysis.installed_software_refs
documents.text: malware-analysis.installed_software_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Any non-standard software installed on the operating system (specified through the operating-system value) used for the dynamic analysis of the malware instance or family. The value of this property MUST be the identifier for a SCO software object.

documents.title: malware-analysis.configuration_version
documents.text: malware-analysis.configuration_version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The named configuration of additional product configuration parameters for this analysis run. For example, when a product is configured to do full depth analysis of Window™ PE files. This configuration may have a named version and that named version can be captured in this property. This will ensure additional runs can be configured in the same way.

documents.title: malware-analysis.modules
documents.text: malware-analysis.modules has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. The specific analysis modules that were used and configured in the product during this analysis run. For example, configuring a product to support analysis of Dridex.

documents.title: malware-analysis.analysis_engine_version
documents.text: malware-analysis.analysis_engine_version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The version of the analysis engine or product (including AV engines) that was used to perform the analysis.

documents.title: malware-analysis.analysis_definition_version
documents.text: malware-analysis.analysis_definition_version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The version of the analysis definitions used by the analysis tool (including AV tools).

documents.title: malware-analysis.submitted
documents.text: malware-analysis.submitted has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The date and time that the malware was first submitted for scanning or analysis. This value will stay constant while the scanned date can change. For example, when Malware was submitted to a virus analysis tool.

documents.title: malware-analysis.analysis_started
documents.text: malware-analysis.analysis_started has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The date and time that the malware analysis was initiated.

documents.title: malware-analysis.analysis_ended
documents.text: malware-analysis.analysis_ended has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The date and time that the malware analysis ended.

documents.title: malware-analysis.result_name
documents.text: malware-analysis.result_name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The classification result or name assigned to the malware instance by the scanner tool.

documents.title: malware-analysis.result
documents.text: malware-analysis.result has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The classification result as determined by the scanner or tool analysis process. The value for this property SHOULD come from the malware-result-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: malware-analysis.analysis_sco_refs
documents.text: malware-analysis.analysis_sco_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. This property contains the references to the STIX Cyber-observable Objects that were captured during the analysis process.

documents.title: malware-analysis.sample_ref
documents.text: malware-analysis.sample_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. This property contains the reference to the SCO file, network traffic or artifact object that this malware analysis was performed against. Caution should be observed when creating an SRO between Malware and Malware Analysis objects when the Malware sample_refs property does not contain the SCO that is included in the Malware Analysis sample_ref property. Note, this property can also contain a reference to an SCO which is not associated with Malware (i.e., some SCO which was scanned and found to be benign.)

documents.title: malware-analysis: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for malware-analysis are: created, id, modified, product, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: note: overview
documents.text: A Note is intended to convey informative text to provide further context and/or to provide additional analysis not contained in the STIX Objects, Marking Definition objects, or Language Content objects which the Note relates to. Notes can be created by anyone (not just the original object creator). For example, an analyst may add a Note to a Campaign object created by another organization indicating that they've seen posts related to that Campaign on a hacker forum.

documents.title: note.type
documents.text: note.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be note

documents.title: note.abstract
documents.text: note.abstract has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A brief summary of the note content.

documents.title: note.content
documents.text: note.content has type string. Its property-table status is required. The content of the note.

documents.title: note.authors
documents.text: note.authors has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. The name of the author(s) of this note (e.g., the analyst(s) that created it).

documents.title: note.object_refs
documents.text: note.object_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is required. The STIX Objects that the note is being applied to.

documents.title: note: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for note are: content, created, id, modified, object_refs, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: observed-data: overview
documents.text: Observed Data conveys information about cyber security related entities such as files, systems, and networks using the STIX Cyber-observable Objects (SCOs). For example, Observed Data can capture information about an IP address, a network connection, a file, or a registry key. Observed Data is not an intelligence assertion, it is simply the raw information without any context for what it means. Observed Data can capture that a piece of information was seen one or more times. Meaning, it can capture both a single observation of a single entity (file, network connection) as well as the aggregation of multiple observations of an entity. When the number_observed property is 1 the Observed Data represents a single entity. When the number_observed property is greater than 1 , the Observed Data represents several instances of an entity potentially collected over a period of time. If a time window is known, that can be captured using the first_observed and last_observed properties. When used to collect aggregate data, it is likely that some properties in the SCO (e.g., timestamp properties) will be omitted because they would differ for each of the individual observations.

documents.title: observed-data.type
documents.text: observed-data.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be observed-data .

documents.title: observed-data.first_observed
documents.text: observed-data.first_observed has type timestamp. Its property-table status is required. The beginning of the time window during which the data was seen.

documents.title: observed-data.last_observed
documents.text: observed-data.last_observed has type timestamp. Its property-table status is required. The end of the time window during which the data was seen. This MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the first_observed property.

documents.title: observed-data.number_observed
documents.text: observed-data.number_observed has type integer. Its property-table status is required. The number of times that each Cyber-observable object represented in the objects or object_ref property was seen. If present, this MUST be an integer between 1 and 999,999,999 inclusive. If the number_observed property is greater than 1 , the data contained in the objects or object_refs property was seen multiple times. In these cases, object creators MAY omit properties of the SCO (such as timestamps) that are specific to a single instance of that observed data.

documents.title: observed-data.objects
documents.text: observed-data.objects has type observable-container. Its property-table status is optional - deprecated. A dictionary of SCO representing the observation. The dictionary MUST contain at least one object. The cyber observable content MAY include multiple objects if those objects are related as part of a single observation. Multiple objects not related to each other via cyber observable Relationships MUST NOT be contained within the same Observed Data instance. This property MUST NOT be present if object_refs is provided. For example, a Network Traffic object and two IPv4 Address objects related via the src_ref and dst_ref properties can be contained in the same Observed Data because they are all related and used to characterize that single entity. NOTE: this property is now deprecated in favor of object_refs and will be removed in a future version.

documents.title: observed-data.object_refs
documents.text: observed-data.object_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. A list of SCOs and SROs representing the observation. The object_refs MUST contain at least one SCO reference if defined. The object_refs MAY include multiple SCOs and their corresponding SROs, if those SCOs are related as part of a single observation. For example, a Network Traffic object and two IPv4 Address objects related via the src_ref and dst_ref properties can be contained in the same Observed Data because they are all related and used to characterize that single entity. This property MUST NOT be present if objects is provided.

documents.title: observed-data: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for observed-data are: created, first_observed, id, last_observed, modified, number_observed, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: opinion: overview
documents.text: Type Name : opinion An Opinion is an assessment of the correctness of the information in a STIX Object produced by a different entity. The primary property is the opinion property, which captures the level of agreement or disagreement using a fixed scale. That fixed scale also supports a numeric mapping to allow for consistent statistical operations across opinions.

documents.title: opinion.type
documents.text: opinion.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be opinion

documents.title: opinion.explanation
documents.text: opinion.explanation has type string. Its property-table status is optional. An explanation of why the producer has this Opinion. For example, if an Opinion of strongly-disagree is given, the explanation can contain an explanation of why the Opinion producer disagrees and what evidence they have for their disagreement.

documents.title: opinion.authors
documents.text: opinion.authors has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. The name of the author(s) of this Opinion (e.g., the analyst(s) that created it).

documents.title: opinion.opinion
documents.text: opinion.opinion has type enum. Its property-table status is required. The opinion that the producer has about all of the STIX Object(s) listed in the object_refs property. The values of this property MUST come from the opinion-enum enumeration.

documents.title: opinion.object_refs
documents.text: opinion.object_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is required. The STIX Objects that the Opinion is being applied to.

documents.title: opinion: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for opinion are: created, id, modified, object_refs, opinion, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: report: overview
documents.text: Reports are collections of threat intelligence focused on one or more topics, such as a description of a threat actor, malware, or attack technique, including context and related details. They are used to group related threat intelligence together so that it can be published as a comprehensive cyber threat story. The Report SDO contains a list of references to STIX Objects (the CTI objects included in the report) along with a textual description and the name of the report.

documents.title: report.type
documents.text: report.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be report .

documents.title: report.name
documents.text: report.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify the Report.

documents.title: report.description
documents.text: report.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Report, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: report.report_types
documents.text: report.report_types has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The primary type(s) of content found in this report. The values for this property SHOULD come from the report-type-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: report.published
documents.text: report.published has type timestamp. Its property-table status is required. The date that this Report object was officially published by the creator of this report. The publication date (public release, legal release, etc.) may be different than the date the report was created or shared internally (the date in the created property).

documents.title: report.object_refs
documents.text: report.object_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the STIX Objects that are referred to by this Report.

documents.title: report: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for report are: created, id, modified, name, object_refs, published, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: threat-actor: overview
documents.text: Threat Actors are actual individuals, groups, or organizations believed to be operating with malicious intent. A Threat Actor is not an Intrusion Set but may support or be affiliated with various Intrusion Sets, groups, or organizations over time. Threat Actors leverage their resources, and possibly the resources of an Intrusion Set, to conduct attacks and run Campaigns against targets.

documents.title: threat-actor.type
documents.text: threat-actor.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be threat-actor .

documents.title: threat-actor.name
documents.text: threat-actor.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify this Threat Actor or Threat Actor group.

documents.title: threat-actor.description
documents.text: threat-actor.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Threat Actor, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: threat-actor.threat_actor_types
documents.text: threat-actor.threat_actor_types has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The type(s) of this threat actor. The values for this property SHOULD come from the threat-actor-type-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: threat-actor.aliases
documents.text: threat-actor.aliases has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. A list of other names that this Threat Actor is believed to use.

documents.title: threat-actor.first_seen
documents.text: threat-actor.first_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Threat Actor was first seen. This property is a summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are earlier than the first seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data.

documents.title: threat-actor.last_seen
documents.text: threat-actor.last_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The time that this Threat Actor was last seen. This property is a summary property of data from sightings and other data that may or may not be available in STIX. If new sightings are received that are later than the last seen timestamp, the object may be updated to account for the new data. If this property and the first_seen property are both defined, then this property MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the first_seen property.

documents.title: threat-actor.roles
documents.text: threat-actor.roles has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. A list of roles the Threat Actor plays. The values for this property SHOULD come from the threat-actor-role-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: threat-actor.goals
documents.text: threat-actor.goals has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. The high-level goals of this Threat Actor, namely, what are they trying to do. For example, they may be motivated by personal gain, but their goal is to steal credit card numbers. To do this, they may execute specific Campaigns that have detailed objectives like compromising point of sale systems at a large retailer.

documents.title: threat-actor.sophistication
documents.text: threat-actor.sophistication has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The skill, specific knowledge, special training, or expertise a Threat Actor must have to perform the attack. The value for this property SHOULD come from the threat-actor-sophistication-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: threat-actor.resource_level
documents.text: threat-actor.resource_level has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The organizational level at which this Threat Actor typically works, which in turn determines the resources available to this Threat Actor for use in an attack. This attribute is linked to the sophistication property — a specific resource level implies that the Threat Actor has access to at least a specific sophistication level. The value for this property SHOULD come from the attack-resource-level-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: threat-actor.primary_motivation
documents.text: threat-actor.primary_motivation has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The primary reason, motivation, or purpose behind this Threat Actor. The motivation is why the Threat Actor wishes to achieve the goal (what they are trying to achieve). For example, a Threat Actor with a goal to disrupt the finance sector in a country might be motivated by ideological hatred of capitalism. The value for this property SHOULD come from the attack-motivation-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: threat-actor.secondary_motivations
documents.text: threat-actor.secondary_motivations has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. This property specifies the secondary reasons, motivations, or purposes behind this Threat Actor. These motivations can exist as an equal or near-equal cause to the primary motivation. However, it does not replace or necessarily magnify the primary motivation, but it might indicate additional context. The position in the list has no significance. The value for this property SHOULD come from the attack-motivation-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: threat-actor.personal_motivations
documents.text: threat-actor.personal_motivations has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The personal reasons, motivations, or purposes of the Threat Actor regardless of organizational goals. Personal motivation, which is independent of the organization’s goals, describes what impels an individual to carry out an attack. Personal motivation may align with the organization’s motivation—as is common with activists—but more often it supports personal goals. For example, an individual analyst may join a Data Miner corporation because his or her skills may align with the corporation’s objectives. But the analyst most likely performs his or her daily work toward those objectives for personal reward in the form of a paycheck. The motivation of personal reward may be even stronger for Threat Actors who commit illegal acts, as it is more difficult for someone to cross that line purely for altruistic reasons. The position in the list has no significance. The values for this property SHOULD come from the attack-motivation-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: threat-actor: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for threat-actor are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: tool: overview
documents.text: Tools are legitimate software that can be used by threat actors to perform attacks. Knowing how and when threat actors use such tools can be important for understanding how campaigns are executed. Unlike malware, these tools or software packages are often found on a system and have legitimate purposes for power users, system administrators, network administrators, or even normal users. Remote access tools (e.g., RDP) and network scanning tools (e.g., Nmap) are examples of Tools that may be used by a Threat Actor during an attack. The Tool SDO characterizes the properties of these software tools and can be used as a basis for making an assertion about how a Threat Actor uses them during an attack. It contains properties to name and describe the tool, a list of Kill Chain Phases the tool can be used to carry out, and the version of the tool.

documents.title: tool.type
documents.text: tool.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be tool .

documents.title: tool.name
documents.text: tool.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. The name used to identify the Tool.

documents.title: tool.description
documents.text: tool.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Tool, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: tool.tool_types
documents.text: tool.tool_types has type list of type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. The kind(s) of tool(s) being described. The values for this property SHOULD come from the tool-type-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: tool.aliases
documents.text: tool.aliases has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Alternative names used to identify this Tool.

documents.title: tool.kill_chain_phases
documents.text: tool.kill_chain_phases has type list of type kill-chain-phase. Its property-table status is optional. The list of kill chain phases for which this Tool can be used.

documents.title: tool.tool_version
documents.text: tool.tool_version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The version identifier associated with the Tool.

documents.title: tool: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for tool are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: vulnerability: overview
documents.text: A Vulnerability is a weakness or defect in the requirements, designs, or implementations of the computational logic (e.g., code) found in software and some hardware components (e.g., firmware) that can be directly exploited to negatively impact the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of that system. CVE is a list of information security vulnerabilities and exposures that provides common names for publicly known problems [CVE ]. For example, if a piece of malware exploits CVE-2015-12345, a Malware object could be linked to a Vulnerability object that references CVE-2015-12345.

documents.title: vulnerability.type
documents.text: vulnerability.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be vulnerability .

documents.title: vulnerability.external_references
documents.text: vulnerability.external_references has type list of type external-reference. Its property-table status is optional. A list of external references which refer to non-STIX information. This property MAY be used to provide one or more Vulnerability identifiers, such as a CVE ID [CVE ]. When specifying a CVE ID, the source_name property of the external reference MUST be set to cve and the external_id property MUST be the exact CVE identifier.

documents.title: vulnerability.name
documents.text: vulnerability.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used to identify the Vulnerability.

documents.title: vulnerability.description
documents.text: vulnerability.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Vulnerability, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: vulnerability: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for vulnerability are: created, id, modified, name, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: relationship: overview
documents.text: The Relationship object is used to link together two SDOs or SCOs in order to describe how they are related to each other. If SDOs and SCOs are considered "nodes" or "vertices" in the graph, the Relationship Objects (SROs) represent "edges". STIX defines many relationship types to link together SDOs and SCOs. These relationships are contained in the "Relationships" table under each SDO and SCO definition. Relationship types defined in the specification SHOULD be used to ensure consistency. An example of a specification-defined relationship is that an indicator indicates a campaign . That relationship type is listed in the Relationships section of the Indicator SDO definition.

documents.title: relationship.type
documents.text: relationship.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be relationship .

documents.title: relationship.relationship_type
documents.text: relationship.relationship_type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The name used to identify the type of Relationship. This value SHOULD be an exact value listed in the relationships for the source and target SDO, but MAY be any string. The value of this property MUST be in ASCII and is limited to characters a–z (lowercase ASCII), 0–9, and hyphen (-).

documents.title: relationship.description
documents.text: relationship.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Relationship, potentially including its purpose and its key characteristics.

documents.title: relationship.source_ref
documents.text: relationship.source_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is required. The id of the source (from) object. The value MUST be an ID reference to an SDO or SCO (i.e., it cannot point to an SRO, Bundle, Language Content, or Marking Definition).

documents.title: relationship.target_ref
documents.text: relationship.target_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is required. The id of the target (to) object. The value MUST be an ID reference to an SDO or SCO (i.e., it cannot point to an SRO, Bundle, Language Content, or Marking Definition).

documents.title: relationship.start_time
documents.text: relationship.start_time has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. This optional timestamp represents the earliest time at which the Relationship between the objects exists. If this property is a future timestamp, at the time the start_time property is defined, then this represents an estimate by the producer of the intelligence of the earliest time at which relationship will be asserted to be true. If it is not specified, then the earliest time at which the relationship between the objects exists is not defined.

documents.title: relationship.stop_time
documents.text: relationship.stop_time has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The latest time at which the Relationship between the objects exists. If this property is a future timestamp, at the time the stop_time property is defined, then this represents an estimate by the producer of the intelligence of the latest time at which relationship will be asserted to be true. If start_time and stop_time are both defined, then stop_time MUST be later than the start_time value. If stop_time is not specified, then the latest time at which the relationship between the objects exists is either not known, not disclosed, or has no defined stop time.

documents.title: relationship: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for relationship are: created, id, modified, relationship_type, source_ref, spec_version, target_ref, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: sighting: overview
documents.text: A Sighting denotes the belief that something in CTI (e.g., an indicator, malware, tool, threat actor, etc.) was seen. Sightings are used to track who and what are being targeted, how attacks are carried out, and to track trends in attack behavior. The Sighting relationship object is a special type of SRO; it is a relationship that contains extra properties not present on the Generic Relationship object. These extra properties are included to represent data specific to sighting relationships (e.g., count , representing how many times something was seen), but for other purposes a Sighting can be thought of as a Relationship with a name of "sighting-of". Sighting is captured as a relationship because you cannot have a sighting unless you have something that has been sighted. Sighting does not make sense without the relationship to what was sighted.

documents.title: sighting.type
documents.text: sighting.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be sighting .

documents.title: sighting.description
documents.text: sighting.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A description that provides more details and context about the Sighting.

documents.title: sighting.first_seen
documents.text: sighting.first_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The beginning of the time window during which the SDO referenced by the sighting_of_ref property was sighted.

documents.title: sighting.last_seen
documents.text: sighting.last_seen has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The end of the time window during which the SDO referenced by the sighting_of_ref property was sighted. If this property and the first_seen property are both defined, then this property MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the first_seen property.

documents.title: sighting.count
documents.text: sighting.count has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. If present, this MUST be an integer between 0 and 999,999,999 inclusive and represents the number of times the SDO referenced by the sighting_of_ref property was sighted. Observed Data has a similar property called number_observed , which refers to the number of times the data was observed. These counts refer to different concepts and are distinct. For example, a single sighting of a DDoS bot might have many millions of observations of the network traffic that it generates. Thus, the Sighting count would be 1 (the bot was observed once) but the Observed Data number_observed would be much higher. As another example, a sighting with a count of 0 can be used to express that an indicator was not seen at all.

documents.title: sighting.sighting_of_ref
documents.text: sighting.sighting_of_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is required. An ID reference to the SDO that was sighted (e.g., Indicator or Malware). For example, if this is a Sighting of an Indicator, that Indicator’s ID would be the value of this property. This property MUST reference only an SDO.

documents.title: sighting.observed_data_refs
documents.text: sighting.observed_data_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. A list of ID references to the Observed Data objects that contain the raw cyber data for this Sighting. For example, a Sighting of an Indicator with an IP address could include the Observed Data for the network connection that the Indicator was used to detect. This property MUST reference only Observed Data SDOs.

documents.title: sighting.where_sighted_refs
documents.text: sighting.where_sighted_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. A list of ID references to the Identity or Location objects describing the entities or types of entities that saw the sighting. Omitting the where_sighted_refs property does not imply that the sighting was seen by the object creator. To indicate that the sighting was seen by the object creator, an Identity representing the object creator should be listed in where_sighted_refs . This property MUST reference only Identity or Location SDOs.

documents.title: sighting.summary
documents.text: sighting.summary has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. The summary property indicates whether the Sighting should be considered summary data. Summary data is an aggregation of previous Sightings reports and should not be considered primary source data. Default value is false .

documents.title: sighting: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for sighting are: created, id, modified, sighting_of_ref, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: artifact: overview
documents.text: The Artifact object permits capturing an array of bytes (8-bits), as a base64-encoded string, or linking to a file-like payload. One of payload_bin or url MUST be provided. It is incumbent on object creators to ensure that the URL is accessible for downstream consumers.

documents.title: artifact.type
documents.text: artifact.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be artifact .

documents.title: artifact.mime_type
documents.text: artifact.mime_type has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Whenever feasible, this value SHOULD be one of the values defined in the Template column in the IANA media type registry [Media Types] . Maintaining a comprehensive universal catalog of all extant file types is obviously not possible. When specifying a MIME Type not included in the IANA registry, implementers should use their best judgement so as to facilitate interoperability.

documents.title: artifact.payload_bin
documents.text: artifact.payload_bin has type binary. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the binary data contained in the artifact as a base64-encoded string. This property MUST NOT be present if url is provided.

documents.title: artifact.url
documents.text: artifact.url has type string. Its property-table status is optional. The value of this property MUST be a valid URL that resolves to the unencoded content. This property MUST NOT be present if payload_bin is provided.

documents.title: artifact.hashes
documents.text: artifact.hashes has type hashes. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a dictionary of hashes for the contents of the url or the payload_bin . This property MUST be present when the url property is present. Dictionary keys MUST come from the hash-algorithm-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: artifact.encryption_algorithm
documents.text: artifact.encryption_algorithm has type enum. Its property-table status is optional. If the artifact is encrypted, specifies the type of encryption algorithm the binary data (either via payload_bin or url ) is encoded in. The value of this property MUST come from the encryption-algorithm-enum enumeration. If both mime_type and encryption_algorithm are included, this signifies that the artifact represents an encrypted archive.

documents.title: artifact.decryption_key
documents.text: artifact.decryption_key has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the decryption key for the encrypted binary data (either via payload_bin or url ) . For example, this may be useful in cases of sharing malware samples, which are often encoded in an encrypted archive. This property MUST NOT be present when the encryption_algorithm property is absent.

documents.title: artifact: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for artifact are: id, type. Exactly one of payload_bin or url MUST be supplied. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: autonomous-system: overview
documents.text: This object represents the properties of an Autonomous System (AS).

documents.title: autonomous-system.type
documents.text: autonomous-system.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be autonomous-system .

documents.title: autonomous-system.number
documents.text: autonomous-system.number has type integer. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the number assigned to the AS. Such assignments are typically performed by a Regional Internet Registry (RIR).

documents.title: autonomous-system.name
documents.text: autonomous-system.name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the AS.

documents.title: autonomous-system.rir
documents.text: autonomous-system.rir has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the Regional Internet Registry (RIR) that assigned the number to the AS.

documents.title: autonomous-system: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for autonomous-system are: id, number, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: directory: overview
documents.text: The Directory object represents the properties common to a file system directory.

documents.title: directory.type
documents.text: directory.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be directory .

documents.title: directory.path
documents.text: directory.path has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the path, as originally observed, to the directory on the file system.

documents.title: directory.path_enc
documents.text: directory.path_enc has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the observed encoding for the path. The value MUST be specified if the path is stored in a non-Unicode encoding. This value MUST be specified using the corresponding name from the 2013-12-20 revision of the IANA character set registry [Character Sets ]. If the preferred MIME name for a character set is defined, this value MUST be used; if it is not defined, then the Name value from the registry MUST be used instead.

documents.title: directory.ctime
documents.text: directory.ctime has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the directory was created.

documents.title: directory.mtime
documents.text: directory.mtime has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the directory was last written to/modified.

documents.title: directory.atime
documents.text: directory.atime has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the directory was last accessed.

documents.title: directory.contains_refs
documents.text: directory.contains_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of references to other File and/or Directory objects contained within the directory. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type file or directory .

documents.title: directory: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for directory are: id, path, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: domain-name: overview
documents.text: The Domain Name object represents the properties of a network domain name.

documents.title: domain-name.type
