documents.text: domain-name.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be domain-name .

documents.title: domain-name.value
documents.text: domain-name.value has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the value of the domain name. The value of this property MUST conform to [RFC1034 ], and each domain and sub-domain contained within the domain name MUST conform to [RFC5890 ].

documents.title: domain-name.resolves_to_refs
documents.text: domain-name.resolves_to_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of references to one or more IP addresses or domain names that the domain name resolves to. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type ipv4-addr or ipv6-addr or domain-name (for cases such as CNAME records).

documents.title: domain-name: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for domain-name are: id, type, value. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: email-addr: overview
documents.text: The Email Address object represents a single email address.

documents.title: email-addr.type
documents.text: email-addr.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be email-addr .

documents.title: email-addr.value
documents.text: email-addr.value has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the value of the email address. This MUST NOT include the display name. This property corresponds to the addr-spec construction in section 3.4 of [RFC5322 ], for example, [email protected] .

documents.title: email-addr.display_name
documents.text: email-addr.display_name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a single email display name, i.e., the name that is displayed to the human user of a mail application. This property corresponds to the display-name construction in section 3.4 of [RFC5322 ], for example, Jane Smith .

documents.title: email-addr.belongs_to_ref
documents.text: email-addr.belongs_to_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the user account that the email address belongs to, as a reference to a User Account object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type user-account .

documents.title: email-addr: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for email-addr are: id, type, value. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: email-message: overview
documents.text: The Email Message object represents an instance of an email message, corresponding to the internet message format described in [RFC5322 ] and related RFCs. Header field values that have been encoded as described in section 2 of [RFC2047 ] MUST be decoded before inclusion in Email Message object properties. For example, this is some text MUST be used instead of =?iso-8859-1?q?this=20is=20some=20text?= . Any characters in the encoded value which cannot be decoded into Unicode SHOULD be replaced with the 'REPLACEMENT CHARACTER' (U+FFFD). If it is necessary to capture the header value as observed, this can be achieved by referencing an Artifact object through the raw_email_ref property.

documents.title: email-message.type
documents.text: email-message.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be email-message .

documents.title: email-message.is_multipart
documents.text: email-message.is_multipart has type boolean. Its property-table status is required. Indicates whether the email body contains multiple MIME parts.

documents.title: email-message.date
documents.text: email-message.date has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time that the email message was sent.

documents.title: email-message.content_type
documents.text: email-message.content_type has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the value of the "Content-Type" header of the email message.

documents.title: email-message.from_ref
documents.text: email-message.from_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the value of the "From:" header of the email message. The "From:" field specifies the author of the message, that is, the mailbox(es) of the person or system responsible for the writing of the message. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type email-address .

documents.title: email-message.sender_ref
documents.text: email-message.sender_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the value of the "Sender" field of the email message. The "Sender:" field specifies the mailbox of the agent responsible for the actual transmission of the message. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type email-address .

documents.title: email-message.to_refs
documents.text: email-message.to_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the mailboxes that are "To:" recipients of the email message. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type email-address .

documents.title: email-message.cc_refs
documents.text: email-message.cc_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the mailboxes that are "CC:" recipients of the email message. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type email-address .

documents.title: email-message.bcc_refs
documents.text: email-message.bcc_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the mailboxes that are "BCC:" recipients of the email message. As per [RFC5322 ], the absence of this property should not be interpreted as semantically equivalent to an absent BCC header on the message being characterized. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type email-address .

documents.title: email-message.message_id
documents.text: email-message.message_id has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the Message-ID field of the email message.

documents.title: email-message.subject
documents.text: email-message.subject has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the subject of the email message.

documents.title: email-message.received_lines
documents.text: email-message.received_lines has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies one or more "Received" header fields that may be included in the email headers. List values MUST appear in the same order as present in the email message.

documents.title: email-message.additional_header_fields
documents.text: email-message.additional_header_fields has type dictionary. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies any other header fields (except for date , received_lines , content_type , from_ref , sender_ref , to_refs , cc_refs , bcc_refs , and subject ) found in the email message, as a dictionary. Each key/value pair in the dictionary represents the name/value of a single header field or names/values of a header field that occurs more than once. Each dictionary key SHOULD be a case-preserved version of the header field name. The corresponding value for each dictionary key MUST always be a list of type string to support when a header field is repeated.

documents.title: email-message.body
documents.text: email-message.body has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a string containing the email body. This property MUST NOT be used if is_multipart is true.

documents.title: email-message.body_multipart
documents.text: email-message.body_multipart has type list of type email-mime-part-type. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of the MIME parts that make up the email body. This property MUST NOT be used if is_multipart is false.

documents.title: email-message.raw_email_ref
documents.text: email-message.raw_email_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the raw binary contents of the email message, including both the headers and body, as a reference to an Artifact object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type artifact .

documents.title: email-message: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for email-message are: id, is_multipart, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: file: overview
documents.text: The File object represents the properties of a file. A File object MUST contain at least one of hashes or name .

documents.title: file.type
documents.text: file.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be file .

documents.title: file.extensions
documents.text: file.extensions has type dictionary. Its property-table status is optional. The File object defines the following extensions. In addition to these, producers MAY create their own. ntfs-ext , raster-image-ext , pdf-ext , archive-ext , windows-pebinary-ext Dictionary keys MUST use the specification defined name (examples above) or be the id of a STIX Extension object, depending on the type of extension being used. The corresponding dictionary values MUST contain the contents of the extension instance.

documents.title: file.hashes
documents.text: file.hashes has type hashes. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a dictionary of hashes for the file. (When used with the Archive File Extension, this refers to the hash of the entire archive file, not its contents.) Dictionary keys MUST come from the hash-algorithm-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: file.size
documents.text: file.size has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the size of the file, in bytes. The value of this property MUST NOT be negative.

documents.title: file.name
documents.text: file.name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the file.

documents.title: file.name_enc
documents.text: file.name_enc has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the observed encoding for the name of the file. This value MUST be specified using the corresponding name from the 2013-12-20 revision of the IANA character set registry [Character Sets ]. If the value from the Preferred MIME Name column for a character set is defined, this value MUST be used; if it is not defined, then the value from the Name column in the registry MUST be used instead. This property allows for the capture of the original text encoding for the file name, which may be forensically relevant; for example, a file on an NTFS volume whose name was created using the windows-1251 encoding, commonly used for languages based on Cyrillic script.

documents.title: file.magic_number_hex
documents.text: file.magic_number_hex has type hex. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the hexadecimal constant ("magic number") associated with a specific file format that corresponds to the file, if applicable.

documents.title: file.mime_type
documents.text: file.mime_type has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the MIME type name specified for the file, e.g., application/msword . Whenever feasible, this value SHOULD be one of the values defined in the Template column in the IANA media type registry [Media Types] . Maintaining a comprehensive universal catalog of all extant file types is obviously not possible. When specifying a MIME Type not included in the IANA registry, implementers should use their best judgement so as to facilitate interoperability.

documents.title: file.ctime
documents.text: file.ctime has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the file was created.

documents.title: file.mtime
documents.text: file.mtime has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the file was last written to/modified.

documents.title: file.atime
documents.text: file.atime has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the file was last accessed.

documents.title: file.parent_directory_ref
documents.text: file.parent_directory_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the parent directory of the file, as a reference to a Directory object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type directory .

documents.title: file.contains_refs
documents.text: file.contains_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of references to other Cyber-observable Objects contained within the file, such as another file that is appended to the end of the file, or an IP address that is contained somewhere in the file. This is intended for use cases other than those targeted by the Archive extension.

documents.title: file.content_ref
documents.text: file.content_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the content of the file, represented as an Artifact object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type artifact .

documents.title: file: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for file are: id, type. At least one of hashes or name MUST be supplied. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: ipv4-addr: overview
documents.text: The IPv4 Address object represents one or more IPv4 addresses expressed using CIDR notation.

documents.title: ipv4-addr.type
documents.text: ipv4-addr.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be ipv4-addr .

documents.title: ipv4-addr.value
documents.text: ipv4-addr.value has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the values of one or more IPv4 addresses expressed using CIDR notation. If a given IPv4 Address object represents a single IPv4 address, the CIDR /32 suffix MAY be omitted. Example: 10.2.4.5/24

documents.title: ipv4-addr.resolves_to_refs
documents.text: ipv4-addr.resolves_to_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of references to one or more Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses that the IPv4 address resolves to. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type mac-addr .

documents.title: ipv4-addr.belongs_to_refs
documents.text: ipv4-addr.belongs_to_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of references to one or more autonomous systems (AS) that the IPv4 address belongs to. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type autonomous-system .

documents.title: ipv4-addr: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for ipv4-addr are: id, type, value. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: ipv6-addr: overview
documents.text: The IPv6 Address object represents one or more IPv6 addresses expressed using CIDR notation.

documents.title: ipv6-addr.type
documents.text: ipv6-addr.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be ipv6-addr .

documents.title: ipv6-addr.value
documents.text: ipv6-addr.value has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the values of one or more IPv6 addresses expressed using CIDR notation. If a given IPv6 Address object represents a single IPv6 address, the CIDR /128 suffix MAY be omitted.

documents.title: ipv6-addr.resolves_to_refs
documents.text: ipv6-addr.resolves_to_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of references to one or more Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses that the IPv6 address resolves to. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type mac-addr .

documents.title: ipv6-addr.belongs_to_refs
documents.text: ipv6-addr.belongs_to_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a list of references to one or more autonomous systems (AS) that the IPv6 address belongs to. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type autonomous-system .

documents.title: ipv6-addr: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for ipv6-addr are: id, type, value. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: mac-addr: overview
documents.text: The MAC Address object represents a single Media Access Control (MAC) address.

documents.title: mac-addr.type
documents.text: mac-addr.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be mac-addr .

documents.title: mac-addr.value
documents.text: mac-addr.value has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the value of a single MAC address. The MAC address value MUST be represented as a single colon-delimited, lowercase MAC-48 address, which MUST include leading zeros for each octet. Example: 00:00:ab:cd:ef:01

documents.title: mac-addr: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for mac-addr are: id, type, value. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: mutex: overview
documents.text: The Mutex object represents the properties of a mutual exclusion (mutex) object.

documents.title: mutex.type
documents.text: mutex.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be mutex .

documents.title: mutex.name
documents.text: mutex.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the name of the mutex object.

documents.title: mutex: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for mutex are: id, name, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: network-traffic: overview
documents.text: The Network Traffic object represents arbitrary network traffic that originates from a source and is addressed to a destination. The network traffic MAY or MAY NOT constitute a valid unicast, multicast, or broadcast network connection. This MAY also include traffic that is not established, such as a SYN flood. To allow for use cases where a source or destination address may be sensitive and not suitable for sharing, such as addresses that are internal to an organization’s network, the source and destination properties ( src_ref and dst_ref , respectively) are defined as optional in the properties table below. However, a Network Traffic object MUST contain the protocols property and at least one of the src_ref or dst_ref properties and SHOULD contain the src_port and dst_port properties.

documents.title: network-traffic.type
documents.text: network-traffic.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be network-traffic .

documents.title: network-traffic.extensions
documents.text: network-traffic.extensions has type dictionary. Its property-table status is optional. The Network Traffic object defines the following extensions. In addition to these, producers MAY create their own. http-request-ext , tcp-ext , icmp-ext , socket-ext Dictionary keys MUST use the specification defined name (examples above) or be the id of a STIX Extension object, depending on the type of extension being used. The corresponding dictionary values MUST contain the contents of the extension instance.

documents.title: network-traffic.start
documents.text: network-traffic.start has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the network traffic was initiated, if known.

documents.title: network-traffic.end
documents.text: network-traffic.end has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time the network traffic ended, if known. If the is_active property is true, then the end property MUST NOT be included. If this property and the start property are both defined, then this property MUST be greater than or equal to the timestamp in the start property.

documents.title: network-traffic.is_active
documents.text: network-traffic.is_active has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. Indicates whether the network traffic is still ongoing. If the end property is provided, this property MUST be false .

documents.title: network-traffic.src_ref
documents.text: network-traffic.src_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the source of the network traffic, as a reference to a Cyber-observable Object. The object referenced MUST be of type ipv4-addr , ipv6-addr , mac-addr , or domain-name (for cases where the IP address for a domain name is unknown).

documents.title: network-traffic.dst_ref
documents.text: network-traffic.dst_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the destination of the network traffic, as a reference to a Cyber-observable Object. The object referenced MUST be of type ipv4-addr , ipv6-addr , mac-addr , or domain-name (for cases where the IP address for a domain name is unknown).

documents.title: network-traffic.src_port
documents.text: network-traffic.src_port has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the source port used in the network traffic, as an integer. The port value MUST be in the range of 0 - 65535.

documents.title: network-traffic.dst_port
documents.text: network-traffic.dst_port has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the destination port used in the network traffic, as an integer. The port value MUST be in the range of 0 - 65535.

documents.title: network-traffic.protocols
documents.text: network-traffic.protocols has type list of type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the protocols observed in the network traffic, along with their corresponding state. Protocols MUST be listed in low to high order, from outer to inner in terms of packet encapsulation. That is, the protocols in the outer level of the packet, such as IP, MUST be listed first. The protocol names SHOULD come from the service names defined in the Service Name column of the IANA Service Name and Port Number Registry [Port Numbers] . In cases where there is variance in the name of a network protocol not included in the IANA Registry, content producers should exercise their best judgement, and it is recommended that lowercase names be used for consistency with the IANA registry. If the protocol extension is present, the corresponding protocol value for that extension SHOULD be listed in this property. Examples: ipv4, tcp, http ipv4, udp ipv6, tcp, http ipv6, tcp, ssl, https

documents.title: network-traffic.src_byte_count
documents.text: network-traffic.src_byte_count has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the number of bytes, as a positive integer, sent from the source to the destination.

documents.title: network-traffic.dst_byte_count
documents.text: network-traffic.dst_byte_count has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the number of bytes, as a positive integer, sent from the destination to the source.

documents.title: network-traffic.src_packets
documents.text: network-traffic.src_packets has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the number of packets, as a positive integer, sent from the source to the destination.

documents.title: network-traffic.dst_packets
documents.text: network-traffic.dst_packets has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the number of packets, as a positive integer, sent from the destination to the source.

documents.title: network-traffic.ipfix
documents.text: network-traffic.ipfix has type dictionary. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies any IP Flow Information Export [IPFIX] data for the traffic, as a dictionary. Each key/value pair in the dictionary represents the name/value of a single IPFIX element. Accordingly, each dictionary key SHOULD be a case-preserved version of the IPFIX element name, e.g., octetDeltaCount . Each dictionary value MUST be either an integer or a string , as well as a valid IPFIX property.

documents.title: network-traffic.src_payload_ref
documents.text: network-traffic.src_payload_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the bytes sent from the source to the destination. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type artifact .

documents.title: network-traffic.dst_payload_ref
documents.text: network-traffic.dst_payload_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the bytes sent from the destination to the source. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type artifact .

documents.title: network-traffic.encapsulates_refs
documents.text: network-traffic.encapsulates_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Links to other network-traffic objects encapsulated by this network-traffic object. The objects referenced in this property MUST be of type network-traffic .

documents.title: network-traffic.encapsulated_by_ref
documents.text: network-traffic.encapsulated_by_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Links to another network-traffic object which encapsulates this object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type network-traffic .

documents.title: network-traffic: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for network-traffic are: id, protocols, type. At least one of src_ref or dst_ref MUST be supplied. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: process: overview
documents.text: The Process object represents common properties of an instance of a computer program as executed on an operating system. A Process object MUST contain at least one property (other than type ) from this object (or one of its extensions).

documents.title: process.type
documents.text: process.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be process .

documents.title: process.extensions
documents.text: process.extensions has type dictionary. Its property-table status is optional. The Process object defines the following extensions. In addition to these, producers MAY create their own. windows-process-ext , windows-service-ext Dictionary keys MUST use the specification defined name (examples above) or be the id of a STIX Extension object, depending on the type of extension being used. The corresponding dictionary values MUST contain the contents of the extension instance.

documents.title: process.is_hidden
documents.text: process.is_hidden has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies whether the process is hidden.

documents.title: process.pid
documents.text: process.pid has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the Process ID, or PID, of the process.

documents.title: process.created_time
documents.text: process.created_time has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date/time at which the process was created.

documents.title: process.cwd
documents.text: process.cwd has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the current working directory of the process.

documents.title: process.command_line
documents.text: process.command_line has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the full command line used in executing the process, including the process name (which may be specified individually via the image_ref.name property) and any arguments.

documents.title: process.environment_variables
documents.text: process.environment_variables has type dictionary. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the list of environment variables associated with the process as a dictionary. Each key in the dictionary MUST be a case preserved version of the name of the environment variable, and each corresponding value MUST be the environment variable value as a string .

documents.title: process.opened_connection_refs
documents.text: process.opened_connection_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the list of network connections opened by the process, as a reference to one or more Network Traffic objects. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type network-traffic .

documents.title: process.creator_user_ref
documents.text: process.creator_user_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the user that created the process, as a reference to a User Account object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type user-account .

documents.title: process.image_ref
documents.text: process.image_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the executable binary that was executed as the process image, as a reference to a File object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type file .

documents.title: process.parent_ref
documents.text: process.parent_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the other process that spawned (i.e. is the parent of) this one, as a reference to a Process object. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type process .

documents.title: process.child_refs
documents.text: process.child_refs has type list of type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the other processes that were spawned by (i.e. children of) this process, as a reference to one or more other Process objects. The objects referenced in this list MUST be of type process .

documents.title: process: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for process are: id, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: software: overview
documents.text: The Software object represents high-level properties associated with software, including software products.

documents.title: software.type
documents.text: software.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be software .

documents.title: software.name
documents.text: software.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the name of the software.

documents.title: software.cpe
documents.text: software.cpe has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the Common Platform Enumeration (CPE) entry for the software, if available. The value for this property MUST be a CPE v2.3 entry from the official NVD CPE Dictionary [NVD ] . While the CPE dictionary does not contain entries for all software, whenever it does contain an identifier for a given instance of software, this property SHOULD be present.

documents.title: software.swid
documents.text: software.swid has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the Software Identification (SWID) Tags [SWID ] entry for the software, if available. The tag attribute, tagId, a globally unique identifier, SHOULD be used as a proxy identifier of the tagged product.

documents.title: software.languages
documents.text: software.languages has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the languages supported by the software. The value of each list member MUST be a language code conformant to [ RFC5646 ].

documents.title: software.vendor
documents.text: software.vendor has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the vendor of the software.

documents.title: software.version
documents.text: software.version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the version of the software.

documents.title: software: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for software are: id, name, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: url: overview
documents.text: The URL object represents the properties of a uniform resource locator (URL).

documents.title: url.type
documents.text: url.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be url .

documents.title: url.value
documents.text: url.value has type string. Its property-table status is required. Specifies the value of the URL. The value of this property MUST conform to [RFC3986 ], more specifically section 1.1.3 with reference to the definition for "Uniform Resource Locator".

documents.title: url: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for url are: id, type, value. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: user-account: overview
documents.text: The User Account object represents an instance of any type of user account, including but not limited to operating system, device, messaging service, and social media platform accounts. As all properties of this object are optional, at least one of the properties defined below MUST be included when using this object.

documents.title: user-account.type
documents.text: user-account.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be user-account .

documents.title: user-account.extensions
documents.text: user-account.extensions has type dictionary. Its property-table status is optional. The User Account object defines the following extensions. In addition to these, producers MAY create their own. unix-account-ext Dictionary keys MUST use the specification defined name (examples above) or be the id of a STIX Extension object, depending on the type of extension being used. The corresponding dictionary values MUST contain the contents of the extension instance.

documents.title: user-account.user_id
documents.text: user-account.user_id has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the identifier of the account. The format of the identifier depends on the system the user account is maintained in, and may be a numeric ID, a GUID, an account name, an email address, etc. The user_id property should be populated with whatever field is the unique identifier for the system the account is a member of. For example, on UNIX systems it would be populated with the UID.

documents.title: user-account.credential
documents.text: user-account.credential has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a cleartext credential. This is only intended to be used in capturing metadata from malware analysis (e.g., a hard-coded domain administrator password that the malware attempts to use for lateral movement) and SHOULD NOT be used for sharing of PII.

documents.title: user-account.account_login
documents.text: user-account.account_login has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the account login string, used in cases where the user_id property specifies something other than what a user would type when they login. For example, in the case of a Unix account with user_id 0, the account_login might be "root".

documents.title: user-account.account_type
documents.text: user-account.account_type has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the type of the account. This is an open vocabulary and values SHOULD come from the account-type-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: user-account.display_name
documents.text: user-account.display_name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the display name of the account, to be shown in user interfaces, if applicable. On Unix, this is equivalent to the GECOS field.

documents.title: user-account.is_service_account
documents.text: user-account.is_service_account has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. Indicates that the account is associated with a network service or system process (daemon), not a specific individual.

documents.title: user-account.is_privileged
documents.text: user-account.is_privileged has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies that the account has elevated privileges (i.e., in the case of root on Unix or the Windows Administrator account).

documents.title: user-account.can_escalate_privs
documents.text: user-account.can_escalate_privs has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies that the account has the ability to escalate privileges (i.e., in the case of sudo on Unix or a Windows Domain Admin account)

documents.title: user-account.is_disabled
documents.text: user-account.is_disabled has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies if the account is disabled.

documents.title: user-account.account_created
documents.text: user-account.account_created has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies when the account was created.

documents.title: user-account.account_expires
documents.text: user-account.account_expires has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the expiration date of the account.

documents.title: user-account.credential_last_changed
documents.text: user-account.credential_last_changed has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies when the account credential was last changed.

documents.title: user-account.account_first_login
documents.text: user-account.account_first_login has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies when the account was first accessed.

documents.title: user-account.account_last_login
documents.text: user-account.account_last_login has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies when the account was last accessed.

documents.title: user-account: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for user-account are: id, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: windows-registry-key: overview
documents.text: The Registry Key object represents the properties of a Windows registry key. As all properties of this object are optional, at least one of the properties defined below MUST be included when using this object.

documents.title: windows-registry-key.type
documents.text: windows-registry-key.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be windows-registry-key .

documents.title: windows-registry-key.key
documents.text: windows-registry-key.key has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the full registry key including the hive. The value of the key, including the hive portion, SHOULD be case-preserved. The hive portion of the key MUST be fully expanded and not truncated; e.g., HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE must be used instead of HKLM.

documents.title: windows-registry-key.values
documents.text: windows-registry-key.values has type list of type windows-registry-value-type. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the values found under the registry key.

documents.title: windows-registry-key.modified_time
documents.text: windows-registry-key.modified_time has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the last date/time that the registry key was modified.

documents.title: windows-registry-key.creator_user_ref
documents.text: windows-registry-key.creator_user_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a reference to the user account that created the registry key. The object referenced in this property MUST be of type user-account .

documents.title: windows-registry-key.number_of_subkeys
documents.text: windows-registry-key.number_of_subkeys has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the number of subkeys contained under the registry key.

documents.title: windows-registry-key: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for windows-registry-key are: id, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: x509-certificate: overview
documents.text: The X.509 Certificate object represents the properties of an X.509 certificate, as defined by ITU recommendation X.509 [X.509] . An X.509 Certificate object MUST contain at least one object specific property (other than type ) from this object.

documents.title: x509-certificate.type
documents.text: x509-certificate.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The value of this property MUST be x509-certificate .

documents.title: x509-certificate.is_self_signed
documents.text: x509-certificate.is_self_signed has type boolean. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies whether the certificate is self-signed, i.e., whether itis signed by the same entity whose identity it certifies.

documents.title: x509-certificate.hashes
documents.text: x509-certificate.hashes has type hashes. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies any hashes that were calculated for the entire contents of the certificate. Dictionary keys MUST come from the hash-algorithm-ov open vocabulary.

documents.title: x509-certificate.version
documents.text: x509-certificate.version has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the version of the encoded certificate.

documents.title: x509-certificate.serial_number
documents.text: x509-certificate.serial_number has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the unique identifier for the certificate, as issued by a specific Certificate Authority.

documents.title: x509-certificate.signature_algorithm
documents.text: x509-certificate.signature_algorithm has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the algorithm used to sign the certificate.

documents.title: x509-certificate.issuer
documents.text: x509-certificate.issuer has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the Certificate Authority that issued the certificate.

documents.title: x509-certificate.validity_not_before
documents.text: x509-certificate.validity_not_before has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date on which the certificate validity period begins.

documents.title: x509-certificate.validity_not_after
documents.text: x509-certificate.validity_not_after has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the date on which the certificate validity period ends.

documents.title: x509-certificate.subject
documents.text: x509-certificate.subject has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the entity associated with the public key stored in the subject public key field of the certificate.

documents.title: x509-certificate.subject_public_key_algorithm
documents.text: x509-certificate.subject_public_key_algorithm has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the name of the algorithm with which to encrypt data being sent to the subject.

documents.title: x509-certificate.subject_public_key_modulus
documents.text: x509-certificate.subject_public_key_modulus has type string. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the modulus portion of the subject’s public RSA key.

documents.title: x509-certificate.subject_public_key_exponent
documents.text: x509-certificate.subject_public_key_exponent has type integer. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies the exponent portion of the subject’s public RSA key, as an integer.

documents.title: x509-certificate.x509_v3_extensions
documents.text: x509-certificate.x509_v3_extensions has type x509-v3-extensions-type. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies any standard X.509 v3 extensions that may be used in the certificate.

documents.title: x509-certificate: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for x509-certificate are: id, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: language-content: overview
documents.text: The Language Content object represents text content for STIX Objects represented in languages other than that of the original object. Language content may be a translation of the original object by a third-party, a first-source translation by the original publisher, or additional official language content provided at the time of creation. Language Content contains two important sets of properties:

documents.title: language-content.type
documents.text: language-content.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The type property identifies the type of object. The value of this property MUST be language-content .

documents.title: language-content.object_ref
documents.text: language-content.object_ref has type identifier. Its property-table status is required. The object_ref property identifies the id of the object that this Language Content applies to. It MUST be the identifier for a STIX Object.

documents.title: language-content.object_modified
documents.text: language-content.object_modified has type timestamp. Its property-table status is optional. The object_modified property identifies the modified time of the object that this Language Content applies to. It MUST be an exact match for the modified time of the STIX Object being referenced.

documents.title: language-content.contents
documents.text: language-content.contents has type dictionary. Its property-table status is required. The contents property contains the actual Language Content (translation). The keys in the dictionary MUST be RFC 5646 language codes for which language content is being provided [RFC5646 ]. The values each consist of a dictionary that mirrors the properties in the target object (identified by object_ref and object_modified ). For example, to provide a translation of the name property on the target object the key in the dictionary would be name . For each key in the nested dictionary: ● If the original property is a string , the corresponding property in the language content object MUST contain a string with the content for that property in the language of the top-level key. ● If the original property is a list , the corresponding property in the translation object must also be a list . Each item in this list recursively maps to the item at the same position in the list contained in the target object. The lists MUST have the same length. ● In the event that translations are only provided for some list items, the untranslated list items MUST be represented by an empty string (""). This indicates to a consumer of the Language Content object that they should interpolate the translated list items in the Language Content object with the corresponding (untranslated) list items from the original object as indicated by the object_ref property. ● If the original property is an object (including dictionaries), the corresponding location in the translation object must also be an object. Each key/value field in this object recursively maps to the object with the same key in the original. The translation object MAY contain only a subset of the translatable fields of the original. Keys that point to non-translatable properties in the target or to properties that do not exist in the target object MUST be ignored.

documents.title: language-content: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for language-content are: contents, created, id, modified, object_ref, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: marking-definition: overview
documents.text: Data markings represent restrictions, permissions, and other guidance for how data can be used and shared. For example, data may be shared with the restriction that it must not be re-shared, or that it must be encrypted at rest. In STIX, data markings are specified using the marking-definition object. These definitions are applied to complete STIX Objects using object markings and to individual properties of STIX Objects via granular markings. Multiple markings can be added to the same object, including both object and granular markings. Some types of marking definitions or trust groups have rules about which markings override other markings or which markings can be additive to other markings. This specification does not define rules for how multiple markings applied to the same object or property should be interpreted.

documents.title: marking-definition.type
documents.text: marking-definition.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The type property identifies the type of object. The value of this property MUST be marking-definition .

documents.title: marking-definition.name
documents.text: marking-definition.name has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A name used to identify the Marking Definition.

documents.title: marking-definition.definition_type
documents.text: marking-definition.definition_type has type open-vocab. Its property-table status is optional - deprecated. The definition_type property identifies the type of Marking Definition. The value of the definition_type property SHOULD be one of the types defined in the subsections below: statement or tlp (see sections 7.2.1.3 and 7.2.1.4 ). Any new marking definitions SHOULD be specified using the extension facility described in section 7.3 . If the extensions property is not present, this propertyMUST be present.

documents.title: marking-definition.definition
documents.text: marking-definition.definition has type <marking object>. Its property-table status is optional - deprecated. The definition property contains the marking object itself (e.g., the TLP marking as defined in section 7.2 .1.4 , the Statement marking as defined in section 7.2 .1.3 ). Any new marking definitions SHOULD be specified using the extension facility described in section 7.3 . If the extensions property is not present, this propertyMUST be present.

documents.title: marking-definition: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for marking-definition are: created, id, spec_version, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: extension-definition: overview
documents.text: The STIX Extension Definition object allows producers of threat intelligence to extend existing STIX objects or to create entirely new STIX objects in a standardized way. This object contains detailed information about the extension and any additional properties and or objects that it defines. This extension mechanism MUST NOT be used to redefine existing standardized objects or properties. If a producer does not include the STIX Extension Definition object with the STIX objects that use it, consumers should refer to section 3.3 for information in resolving references.

documents.title: extension-definition.type
documents.text: extension-definition.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The type property identifies the type of object. The value of this property MUST be extension-definition .

documents.title: extension-definition.name
documents.text: extension-definition.name has type string. Its property-table status is required. A name used for display purposes during execution, development, or debugging.

documents.title: extension-definition.description
documents.text: extension-definition.description has type string. Its property-table status is optional. A detailed explanation of what data the extension conveys and how it is intended to be used. While the description property is optional this property SHOULD be populated. Note that the schema property is the normative definition of the extension, and this property, if present, is for documentation purposes only.

documents.title: extension-definition.schema
documents.text: extension-definition.schema has type string. Its property-table status is required. The normative definition of the extension, either as a URL or as plain text explaining the definition. A URL SHOULD point to a JSON schema or a location that contains information about the schema. NOTE: It is recommended that an external reference be provided to the comprehensive documentation of the extension-definition.

documents.title: extension-definition.version
documents.text: extension-definition.version has type string. Its property-table status is required. The version of this extension. Producers of STIX extensions are encouraged to follow standard semantic versioning procedures where the version number follows the pattern, MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. This will allow consumers to distinguish between the three different levels of compatibility typically identified by such versioning strings. As with all STIX Objects, changing a STIX extension definition could involve STIX versioning. See section 3.6.2 for more information on versioning an object versus creating a new one.

documents.title: extension-definition.extension_types
documents.text: extension-definition.extension_types has type list of type enum. Its property-table status is required. This property specifies one or more extension types contained within this extension. The values for this property MUST come from the extension-type-enum enumeration. When this property includes toplevel-property-extension then the extension_properties property SHOULD include one or more property names.

documents.title: extension-definition.extension_properties
documents.text: extension-definition.extension_properties has type list of type string. Its property-table status is optional. This property contains the list of new property names that are added to an object by an extension. This property MUST only be used when the extension_types property includes a value of toplevel-property-extension . In other words, when new properties are being added at the top-level of an existing object.

documents.title: extension-definition: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for extension-definition are: extension_types, name, schema, type, version. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: bundle: overview
documents.text: A Bundle is a collection of arbitrary STIX Objects grouped together in a single container. A Bundle does not have any semantic meaning and the objects contained within the Bundle are not considered related by virtue of being in the same Bundle. A STIX Bundle Object is not a STIX Object but makes use of the type and id Common Properties. A Bundle is transient, and implementations SHOULD NOT assume that other implementations will treat it as a persistent object or keep any custom properties found on the bundle itself.

documents.title: bundle.type
documents.text: bundle.type has type string. Its property-table status is required. The type property identifies the type of object. The value of this property MUST be bundle .

documents.title: bundle.id
documents.text: bundle.id has type identifier. Its property-table status is required. An identifier for this Bundle. The id property for the Bundle is designed to help tools that may need it for processing, however, tools are not required to store or track it. Tools that consume STIX should not rely on the ability to refer to bundles by ID.

documents.title: bundle.objects
documents.text: bundle.objects has type list of type <STIX Object>. Its property-table status is optional. Specifies a set of one or more STIX Objects. Objects in this list MUST be a STIX Object.

documents.title: bundle: required properties
documents.text: The required properties listed for bundle are: id, type. Conditional constraints on other properties still apply; this list alone does not validate an object.

documents.title: STIX common property type
documents.text: Common property type: string. The type property identifies the type of STIX Object. The value of the type property MUST be the name of one of the types of STIX Objects defined in sections 4 , 5 , 6 , and 7 (e.g., indicator ) or the name of a Custom Object as defined by section 11.2 . Applicability and requirement status depend on the object type.

documents.title: STIX common property spec_version
documents.text: Common property spec_version: string. The version of the STIX specification used to represent this object. The value of this property MUST be 2.1 for STIX Objects defined according to this specification. If objects are found where this property is not present, the implicit value for all STIX Objects other than SCOs is 2.0 . Since SCOs are now top-level objects in STIX 2.1, the default value for SCOs is 2.1 . Applicability and requirement status depend on the object type.

documents.title: attack-pattern.spec_version
documents.text: attack-pattern.spec_version has type string. Its common-property status is required for attack-pattern. The version of the STIX specification used to represent this object. The value of this property MUST be 2.1 for STIX Objects defined according to this specification. If objects are found where this property is not present, the implicit value for all STIX Objects other than SCOs is 2.0 . Since SCOs are now top-level objects in STIX 2.1, the default value for SCOs is 2.1 .

documents.title: campaign.spec_version
documents.text: campaign.spec_version has type string. Its common-property status is required for campaign. The version of the STIX specification used to represent this object. The value of this property MUST be 2.1 for STIX Objects defined according to this specification. If objects are found where this property is not present, the implicit value for all STIX Objects other than SCOs is 2.0 . Since SCOs are now top-level objects in STIX 2.1, the default value for SCOs is 2.1 .

documents.title: course-of-action.spec_version
documents.text: course-of-action.spec_version has type string. Its common-property status is required for course-of-action. The version of the STIX specification used to represent this object. The value of this property MUST be 2.1 for STIX Objects defined according to this specification. If objects are found where this property is not present, the implicit value for all STIX Objects other than SCOs is 2.0 . Since SCOs are now top-level objects in STIX 2.1, the default value for SCOs is 2.1 .

documents.title: grouping.spec_version
documents.text: grouping.spec_version has type string. Its common-property status is required for grouping. The version of the STIX specification used to represent this object. The value of this property MUST be 2.1 for STIX Objects defined according to this specification. If objects are found where this property is not present, the implicit value for all STIX Objects other than SCOs is 2.0 . Since SCOs are now top-level objects in STIX 2.1, the default value for SCOs is 2.1 .

documents.title: identity.spec_version
documents.text: identity.spec_version has type string. Its common-property status is required for identity. The version of the STIX specification used to represent this object. The value of this property MUST be 2.1 for STIX Objects defined according to this specification. If objects are found where this property is not present, the implicit value for all STIX Objects other than SCOs is 2.0 . Since SCOs are now top-level objects in STIX 2.1, the default value for SCOs is 2.1 .

documents.title: incident.spec_version
documents.text: incident.spec_version has type string. Its common-property status is required for incident. The version of the STIX specification used to represent this object. The minimum precision MUST be milliseconds (three digits after the decimal place in seconds), but MAY be more precise. The created property MUST NOT be changed when creating a new version of the object. See section 3.6 for further definition of versioning. Applicability and requirement status depend on the object type.

documents.title: STIX common property confidence
documents.text: Common property confidence: integer. The confidence property identifies the confidence that the creator has in the correctness of their data. The confidence value MUST be a number in the range of 0-100. Appendix A contains a table of normative mappings to other confidence scales that MUST be used when presenting the confidence value in one of those scales. If the confidence property is not present, then the confidence of the content is unspecified. Applicability and requirement status depend on the object type.

documents.title: STIX common property object_marking_refs
documents.text: Common property object_marking_refs: list of type identifier. The object_marking_refs property specifies a list of id properties of marking-definition objects that apply to this object. In some cases, though uncommon, marking definitions themselves may be marked with sharing or handling guidance. In this case, this property MUST NOT contain any references to the same Marking Definition object (i.e., it cannot contain any circular references). documents.title: STIX common property extensions
documents.text: Common property extensions: dictionary. Specifies any extensions of the object, as a dictionary. Dictionary keys SHOULD be the id of a STIX Extension object or the name of a predefined object extension found in this specification, depending on the type of extension being used. The corresponding dictionary values MUST contain the contents of the extension instance. Each extension dictionary MAY contain the property extension_type . The value of this property MUST come from the extension-type-enum enumeration. If the extension_type property is not present, then this is a predefined extension which does not use the extension facility described in section 7.3 . When this extension facility is used the extension_type property MUST be present. Applicability and requirement status depend on the object type.
