documents.title: attack-pattern delivers relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines attack-pattern --delivers--> malware. The source_ref points to attack-pattern; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this Attack Pattern is used to deliver this malware instance (or family).

documents.title: attack-pattern targets relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines attack-pattern --targets--> identity, location, vulnerability. The source_ref points to attack-pattern; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this Attack Pattern typically targets the type of victim, location, or vulnerability represented by the related Identity, Location, or Vulnerability object. For example, a targets Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to an Identity object representing domain administrators means that the form of SQL injection characterized by the Attack Pattern targets domain administrators in order to achieve its objectives. Another example is a Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for SQL injection to a Vulnerability in blogging software means that the particular SQL injection attack exploits that vulnerability.

documents.title: attack-pattern uses relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines attack-pattern --uses--> malware, tool. The source_ref points to attack-pattern; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the related Malware or Tool is used to perform the behavior identified in the Attack Pattern. For example, a uses Relationship linking an Attack Pattern for a distributed denial of service (DDoS) to a Tool for Low Orbit Ion Cannon (LOIC) indicates that the tool can be used to perform those DDoS attacks.

documents.title: campaign attributed-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines campaign --attributed-to--> intrusion-set, threat-actor. The source_ref points to campaign; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set or Threat Actor that is involved in carrying out the Campaign. For example, an attributed-to Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to the Urban Fowl Threat Actor means that the actor carried out or was involved in some of the activity described by the Campaign.

documents.title: campaign compromises relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines campaign --compromises--> infrastructure. The source_ref points to campaign; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Campaign compromises the related Infrastructure.

documents.title: campaign originates-from relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines campaign --originates-from--> location. The source_ref points to campaign; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Campaign originates from the related Location. For example, an originates-from relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to a Location representing North America means that Glass Gazelle appears to originate from or is located in North America.

documents.title: campaign targets relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines campaign --targets--> identity, location, vulnerability. The source_ref points to campaign; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Campaign uses exploits of the related Vulnerability or targets the type of victims described by the related Identity or Location. For example, a targets Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to a Vulnerability in a blogging platform indicates that attacks performed as part of Glass Gazelle often exploit that Vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to an Identity describing the energy sector in the United States means that the Campaign typically carries out attacks against targets in that sector.

documents.title: campaign uses relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines campaign --uses--> attack-pattern, infrastructure, malware, tool. The source_ref points to campaign; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that attacks carried out as part of the Campaign typically use the related Attack Pattern, Infrastructure, Malware, or Tool. For example, a uses Relationship from the Glass Gazelle Campaign to the xInject Malware indicates that xInject is often used during attacks attributed to that Campaign. A campaign, threat actor, intrusion set, malware, or tool takes infrastructure and compromises and/or uses it for their own.

documents.title: course-of-action investigates relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines course-of-action --investigates--> indicator. The source_ref points to course-of-action; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can be used to investigate the Indicator.

documents.title: course-of-action mitigates relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines course-of-action --mitigates--> attack-pattern, indicator, malware, tool, vulnerability. The source_ref points to course-of-action; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can mitigate (e.g. respond to a threat) the related Attack Pattern, Indicator, Malware, Vulnerability, or Tool. For example, a mitigates Relationship from a Course of Action object to a Malware object indicates that the course of action mitigates the malware.

documents.title: course-of-action remediates relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines course-of-action --remediates--> malware, vulnerability. The source_ref points to course-of-action; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Course of Action can be used to remediate (e.g. clean up) the malware or vulnerability

documents.title: identity located-at relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines identity --located-at--> location. The source_ref points to identity; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Identity is located at or in the related Location. For example, a located-at relationship from the ACME Corporation to a Location representing the United States means that ACME Corporation is located in the United States.

documents.title: indicator indicates relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines indicator --indicates--> attack-pattern, campaign, infrastructure, intrusion-set, malware, threat-actor, tool. The source_ref points to indicator; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Indicator can detect evidence of the related Attack Pattern, Campaign, Infrastructure, Intrusion Set, Malware, Threat Actor, or Tool. This evidence may not be direct: for example, the Indicator may detect secondary evidence of the Campaign, such as malware or behavior commonly used by that Campaign. For example, an indicates Relationship from an Indicator to a Campaign object representing Glass Gazelle means that the Indicator is capable of detecting evidence of Glass Gazelle, such as command and control IPs commonly used by that Campaign.

documents.title: indicator based-on relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines indicator --based-on--> observed-data. The source_ref points to indicator; target_ref points to the target object. This relationship describes that the indicator was created based on information from an observed-data object. For example, an indicator may be created based upon the observation of a spearphishing email or created based upon analysis performed on a piece of malware or adversary infrastructure.

documents.title: infrastructure communicates-with relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --communicates-with--> infrastructure, ipv4-addr, ipv6-addr, domain-name, url. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this infrastructure instance communicates with the defined network addressable resource. For example, a botnet could communicate with a crypto-currency mining pool. This does not mean that the pool is a part of this infrastructure.

documents.title: infrastructure consists-of relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --consists-of--> infrastructure, observed-data, <All STIX Cyber-observable Objects >. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents the objects that are used to make up an infrastructure instance, such as ipv4-addr , ipv6-addr , domain-name , url . An infrastructure instance consists of zero or more objects. While not all SCO types will make sense as infrastructure, allowing any type of SCO prevents artificially restricting what could be used.

documents.title: infrastructure controls relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --controls--> infrastructure, malware. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this infrastructure controls some other infrastructure or a malware instance (or family).

documents.title: infrastructure delivers relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --delivers--> malware. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this infrastructure is used to actively deliver a malware instance (or family).

documents.title: infrastructure has relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --has--> vulnerability. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this specific Infrastructure has this specific Vulnerability. For example, a web server may not have been patched and currently is impacted by a CVE.

documents.title: infrastructure hosts relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --hosts--> tool, malware. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this infrastructure has a tool running on it or is used to passively host the tool / malware. For example, an SSH server may be hosted on a piece of infrastructure.

documents.title: infrastructure located-at relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --located-at--> location. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the infrastructure originates from the related location. For example, a located-at relationship from the Red Orca C2 infrastructure to a Location representing North America means that the Red Orca C2 Infrastructure appears to originate from or is located in North America.

documents.title: infrastructure uses relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines infrastructure --uses--> infrastructure. The source_ref points to infrastructure; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this infrastructure uses this other infrastructure to achieve its objectives.

documents.title: intrusion-set attributed-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines intrusion-set --attributed-to--> threat-actor. The source_ref points to intrusion-set; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the related Threat Actor is involved in carrying out the Intrusion Set. For example, an attributed-to Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to the Urban Fowl Threat Actor means that the actor carried out or was involved in some of the activity described by the Intrusion Set.

documents.title: intrusion-set compromises relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines intrusion-set --compromises--> infrastructure. The source_ref points to intrusion-set; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set compromises the related Infrastructure.

documents.title: intrusion-set originates-from relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines intrusion-set --originates-from--> location. The source_ref points to intrusion-set; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set originates from the related location and SHOULD NOT be used to define attribution. For example, an originates-from relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to a Location representing North America means that the Red Orca Intrusion Set appears to originate from or is located in North America.

documents.title: intrusion-set targets relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines intrusion-set --targets--> identity, location, vulnerability. The source_ref points to intrusion-set; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Intrusion Set uses exploits of the related Vulnerability or targets the type of victims described by the related Identity or Location. For example, a targets Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to a Vulnerability in a blogging platform indicates that attacks performed as part of Red Orca often exploit that Vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to an Identity describing the energy sector in the United States means that the Intrusion Set typically carries out attacks against targets in that sector.

documents.title: intrusion-set uses relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines intrusion-set --uses--> attack-pattern, infrastructure, malware, tool. The source_ref points to intrusion-set; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that attacks carried out as part of the Intrusion Set typically use the related Attack Pattern, Infrastructure, Malware, or Tool. For example, a uses Relationship from the Red Orca Intrusion Set to the xInject Malware indicates that xInject is often used during attacks attributed to that Intrusion Set.

documents.title: malware authored-by relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --authored-by--> threat-actor, intrusion-set. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the malware instance or family was developed by the related threat actor or intrusion set.

documents.title: malware communicates-with relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --communicates-with--> ipv4-addr, ipv6-addr, domain-name, url. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this malware instance (or family) communicates with (beacons to, connects to, or exfiltrated data to) the defined network addressable resource.

documents.title: malware controls relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --controls--> malware. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this malware instance (or family) can control other malware which may be resident on the same system on which it is executing. Note that this is not meant to imply or state that the malware instance or family drops other malware (which is covered by the drops relationship). Rather, it is meant to state that the malware instance or family is able to subvert or control other malware to achieve its goals.

documents.title: malware exploits relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --exploits--> vulnerability. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this malware instance or family exploits or attempts to exploit a particular vulnerability. For example, an exploits Relationship linking a malware instance or family representing a downloader to a Vulnerability for CVE-2016-0001 means that the malware instance or family exploits that vulnerability.

documents.title: malware originates-from relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --originates-from--> location. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this malware instance or family originates from a particular location.

documents.title: malware targets relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --targets--> identity, infrastructure, location, vulnerability. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that a malware instance or family is being used to target an Identity, Infrastructure, or Location. For malware families, this can be used to capture the full set of identities, infrastructures, or locations targeted by the family. Similarly, a targets Relationship linking a malware instance or family representing a downloader to an Identity representing the energy sector means that downloader is typically used against targets in the energy sector.

documents.title: malware uses relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --uses--> attack-pattern, infrastructure, malware, tool. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this malware instance or family uses the attack pattern, infrastructure, malware, or tool to achieve its objectives. For example, a uses Relationship from the jay-sm17h Threat Actor to the xInject Malware indicates that xInject is often used by jay-sm17h.

documents.title: malware variant-of relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware --variant-of--> malware. The source_ref points to malware; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship is used to document that one malware instance or family is a variant of another malware instance or family. Only the following uses of this relationship are valid: Malware instance → Malware family: a Malware instance is a variant of a Malware family. For example, a particular Zeus version 2 sample is a variant of the broader Zeus family. Malware family → Malware family: a Malware family is a variant of another Malware family. For example, the Gameover Zeus family is a variant of the broader Zeus family. Malware instance → Malware instance: a Malware instance is a variant of another Malware instance. For example, a particular Cryptolocker instance that is based on an another Cryptolocker instance with minor changes. Malware family → Malware instance: this relationship MUST NOT be used as it is not semantically valid.

documents.title: malware-analysis characterizes relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware-analysis --characterizes--> malware. The source_ref points to malware-analysis; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the malware analysis describes the related malware.

documents.title: malware-analysis analysis-of relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware-analysis --analysis-of--> malware. The source_ref points to malware-analysis; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the malware analysis is results for the related malware.

documents.title: malware-analysis static-analysis-of relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware-analysis --static-analysis-of--> malware. The source_ref points to malware-analysis; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the malware analysis is static analysis results for the related malware.

documents.title: malware-analysis dynamic-analysis-of relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines malware-analysis --dynamic-analysis-of--> malware. The source_ref points to malware-analysis; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the malware analysis is dynamic analysis results for the related malware.

documents.title: threat-actor attributed-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines threat-actor --attributed-to--> identity. The source_ref points to threat-actor; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Threat Actor's real identity is the related Identity. For example, an attributed-to Relationship from the jay-sm17h Threat Actor to the John Smith Identity means that the actor known as jay-sm17h is John Smith.

documents.title: threat-actor compromises relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines threat-actor --compromises--> infrastructure. The source_ref points to threat-actor; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Threat Actor compromises the related Infrastructure.

documents.title: threat-actor impersonates relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines threat-actor --impersonates--> identity. The source_ref points to threat-actor; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Threat Actor impersonates the related Identity. For example, an impersonates Relationship from the gh0st Threat Actor to the ACME Corp. Identity means that the actor known as gh0st impersonates ACME Corp.

documents.title: threat-actor located-at relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines threat-actor --located-at--> location. The source_ref points to threat-actor; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Threat Actor is located at or in the related Location. For example, a located-at relationship from the gh0st Threat Actor to a Location representing the United States means that ACME Corporation is located in the United States.

documents.title: threat-actor targets relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines threat-actor --targets--> identity, location, vulnerability. The source_ref points to threat-actor; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that the Threat Actor uses exploits of the related Vulnerability or targets the type of victims described by the related Identity or Location. For example, a targets Relationship from the jay-sm17h Threat Actor to a Vulnerability in a blogging platform indicates that attacks performed by John Smith often exploit that Vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship from the jay-sm17h Threat Actor to an Identity describing the energy sector in the United States means that John Smith often carries out attacks against targets in that sector.

documents.title: threat-actor uses relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines threat-actor --uses--> attack-pattern, infrastructure, malware, tool. The source_ref points to threat-actor; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that attacks carried out as part of the Threat Actor typically use the related Attack Pattern, Infrastructure, Malware, or Tool. For example, a uses Relationship from the jay-sm17h Threat Actor to the xInject Malware indicates that xInject is often used by John Smith. A campaign, threat actor, intrusion set, malware, or tool takes infrastructure and compromises and/or uses it for their own.

documents.title: tool delivers relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines tool --delivers--> malware. The source_ref points to tool; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this Tool is used to deliver a malware instance (or family).

documents.title: tool drops relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines tool --drops--> malware. The source_ref points to tool; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this Tool drops a malware instance (or family).

documents.title: tool has relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines tool --has--> vulnerability. The source_ref points to tool; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this specific Tool has this specific Vulnerability. For example, a tool may not have been patched and currently is impacted by a CVE.

documents.title: tool targets relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines tool --targets--> identity, infrastructure, location, vulnerability. The source_ref points to tool; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship documents that this Tool is being used to target this Identity, Infrastructure, Location, or exploit the Vulnerability. For example, a targets Relationship linking an exploit Tool to a Vulnerability for CVE-2016-0001 means that the tool exploits that vulnerability. Similarly, a targets Relationship linking a DDoS Tool to an Identity representing the energy sector means that Tool is typically used against targets in the energy sector.

documents.title: tool uses relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines tool --uses--> infrastructure. The source_ref points to tool; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this Tool uses the related Infrastructure.

documents.title: domain-name resolves-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines domain-name --resolves-to--> domain-name, ipv4-addr, ipv6-addr. The source_ref points to domain-name; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this Domain Name resolves to one or more IP addresses or domain names.

documents.title: ipv4-addr resolves-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines ipv4-addr --resolves-to--> mac-addr. The source_ref points to ipv4-addr; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this IPv4 Address resolves to one or more Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses.

documents.title: ipv4-addr belongs-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines ipv4-addr --belongs-to--> autonomous-system. The source_ref points to ipv4-addr; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this IPv4 Address belongs to one or more autonomous systems (AS).

documents.title: ipv6-addr resolves-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines ipv6-addr --resolves-to--> mac-addr. The source_ref points to ipv6-addr; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this IPv6 Address resolves to one or more Layer 2 Media Access Control (MAC) addresses.

documents.title: ipv6-addr belongs-to relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 defines ipv6-addr --belongs-to--> autonomous-system. The source_ref points to ipv6-addr; target_ref points to the target object. This Relationship describes that this IPv6 Address belongs to one or more autonomous systems (AS).

documents.title: STIX relationships
documents.text: Relationships are directed. A relationship object stores relationship_type, source_ref and target_ref. An indicator can indicates malware: source_ref is the indicator ID and target_ref is the malware ID. Embedded *_ref and *_refs properties link objects without a separate relationship object.

documents.title: STIX custom relationships
documents.text: STIX 2.1 permits user-defined relationship_type values. The specification-defined relationship tables are not an exhaustive allowlist of every possible relationship. The common relationships related-to, derived-from and duplicate-of have general meanings.

documents.title: STIX open vocab
documents.text: An open vocabulary provides suggested values and permits other string values. An enumeration restricts values to its defined set. Do not reject a value solely because it is absent from an open vocabulary.

documents.title: STIX schema validation
documents.text: The OASIS JSON schemas are non-normative aids. Passing JSON Schema validation does not prove full STIX 2.1 conformance: cross-property, reference-target, temporal, and pattern semantics also need checks against the normative specification.

documents.title: STIX sdo sco
documents.text: SDOs describe higher-level threat intelligence such as malware, indicators and threat actors. SCOs describe observable entities such as files, IPv4 addresses and network traffic. A Sighting or Observed Data object adds observation context; an SCO by itself is not a sighting.

documents.title: STIX indicator observed
documents.text: An indicator describes a detection pattern and when that pattern is valid. Observed Data describes actual observations of SCOs using object_refs, first_observed, last_observed and number_observed. These are different roles.

documents.title: STIX ids
documents.text: A STIX identifier has the form object-type--UUID. SDOs and SROs SHOULD use UUIDv4. SCOs SHOULD use deterministic UUIDv5 based on their ID-contributing properties and the specified STIX namespace; the exact rules depend on the object type.

documents.title: STIX bundle
documents.text: A bundle is a transport container with required type and id and an optional objects list. It is not an SDO and does not itself convey relationships between the objects it contains. A bundle has no spec_version property; individual versioned STIX objects carry their own version information.

documents.title: STIX versioning
documents.text: Object versions share the same id and created timestamp, while modified identifies the version. modified MUST NOT be earlier than created. Revocation is indicated by revoked: true and is permanent; future versions of that object ID MUST NOT be created. SCOs do not use SDO-style created/modified versioning.

documents.title: STIX timestamps
documents.text: created is the time the object was originally created and stays unchanged across versions. modified is the time of this particular version and MUST be later than or equal to created. Both have at least millisecond precision.

documents.title: STIX markings
documents.text: object_marking_refs applies referenced marking definitions to an object. granular_markings applies markings to selected properties using selectors. Markings describe handling requirements; they do not encrypt the content.

documents.title: STIX patterns
documents.text: A STIX pattern is an expression over observable properties, for example [ipv4-addr:value = '198.51.100.7']. An indicator using STIX pattern syntax sets pattern_type to stix and supplies pattern and valid_from. Other pattern types may use different syntax.

documents.title: STIX extensions
documents.text: An extension-definition describes an extension and its schema, version, extension_types and creator. Extension definitions can describe property extensions or new SDO, SCO or SRO types. A custom property by itself is not a built-in STIX property.
